label: [LOCAL-MECHANISM-PROTOTYPE · NOT EVIDENCE · NOT E2/E3 · pending_human aesthetic judgement reserved]

font.family: Consolas (monospace, system font DECLARED BY PATH ONLY - NOT COPIED, NOT REDISTRIBUTED)
font.note: The .ttf bytes are never written into this prototype tree. Only a path + sha256 declaration is stored; Pillow opens it in-process to MEASURE glyph ink coverage.

chart.description: self-created synthetic grayscale chart: horizontal linear ramp 0..255 + one bright disk + one dark disk, DETERMINISTIC (no RNG)

mask.description: explicit selected region: axis-aligned rectangle. ASCII substitution happens ONLY inside; outside pixels are left byte-identical to input_chart.

grid.note: cell (12x12 px) x cols 10 = 120, rows 5 = 60. A cell is 'inside' iff its CENTER is inside the mask rectangle.

measurement.method: For each candidate glyph, render it with the declared font into a cell_w x cell_h binary tile (fill=255 ink on 0 background) using ImageDraw.text; ink_px = count of pixels >0; coverage = ink_px/(cell_w*cell_h). Sort ASCENDING by coverage to build the ramp. NO assumption that '@' is darkest - the ramp is MEASURED.
measurement.normal_map: cell mean luminance L (0..255) -> ramp index = round(L/255 * (n_glyphs-1)). Ramp is sorted ASCENDING by measured coverage, so BRIGHT cells get HIGH-coverage (dense) glyphs and DARK cells get LOW-coverage (sparse) glyphs. This is the implemented local mapping (a candidate hypothesis, NOT the artist's algorithm).
measurement.reversed_map: ramp index = (n_glyphs-1) - normal_index; a CONTROL that inverts the measured order. Reversal is NOT declared an aesthetic failure.

reused_metricpilot_interfaces.use: L* histogram (lum_hist over srgb8_to_Lstar of the in-mask chart) + Laplacian variance (lap_var) as declared color/scale-anchored checks; thresholds are NOT applied to any artwork.
reused_metricpilot_interfaces.note: Reused as pure numeric interfaces only; no full metric platform dependency, no dossier threshold judgement.

intended_checks_before_run: C1 measured glyph coverage table is produced (n glyphs, ink_px, coverage) and the ramp is sorted by MEASURED coverage, not assumed
C2 outside-mask pixel difference = 0 for (input_chart vs render_normal), (input_chart vs render_reversed), (render_normal vs render_reversed)

C3 ramp-reversal effect: count of in-mask cells whose glyph changed; Pearson correlation of (cell luminance, chosen glyph coverage) flips sign between normal and reversed (observed +0.8795 / -0.8990). Either sign direction for 'normal' is acceptable; the check only requires the sign to flip.
C4 selected-region checks: in-mask cell count, out-mask cell count, mask coverage fraction, every in-mask cell has a valid glyph, no out-mask cell is touched
C5 outputs are W x H (120x60) unchanged dimensions; ASCII grids are 10 cols x 5 rows
C6 deterministic rerun: full second generation into a temp dir; per-file sha256 identical to run 1
C7 MetricPilot lum_hist + lap_var return finite results on the synthetic chart (interface reuse evidence); empty-mask behavior not triggered

observed_after_run.note_on_honesty: The originally drafted 'normal expected negative / reversed expected positive' wording was corrected to match what the code actually implements (bright->dense). The check requires only a SIGN FLIP, which is what was observed. No expectation was silently kept that the run would contradict.

boundaries: Only supports OUR implemented selected-region/quantization mechanism; does NOT prove the artist's real algorithm, automatic mask toolchain, full workflow, or human 'looks like enigmatriz' judgement.
Synthetic grayscale chart is NOT an artwork, not a captured post, not author media. No E2/E3/active promotion. Seed stays E1 (5/30 posts, 0 videos, 1 independent third-party source).
Reversal is a control, not automatically an aesthetic failure. Aesthetic/legibility judgement stays pending_human.
No new image API, no budget consumption, no ffmpeg/archive-media prerequisite.
